title: How to Switch from Arcade to Storylane
summary: A step-by-step guide to migrating your Arcade demos to Storylane: what the migration looks like, how your demos transfer, and what you gain after switching.
body_markdown:
If you've been using Arcade and are ready to move to a more sales-capable demo platform, this guide covers what migration looks like: what happens to your existing demos, the steps to switch, and what changes after.


## Why teams move from Arcade to Storylane


If you're still weighing your options, Storylane's[comparison with Arcade](https://www.storylane.io/blog/storylane-vs-arcade) covers features, pricing, and a clear breakdown of which tool fits which use case.


If you've already decided, the most common reasons teams make the switch are:


- **Screenshot and GIF format limits what prospects can do.** Arcade creates image-based walkthroughs, not interactive HTML demos. Prospects click through a sequence of screenshots rather than experiencing the product itself. For early-stage awareness content, that works. For sales and conversion, it falls short.
- **No lead capture or viewer identification.** Arcade doesn't capture who watched your demo or let you gate it with a lead form. You get share counts, not pipeline signals. Teams that want to know which accounts are engaging, and route that to sales, need something more.
- **Single linear flow only.** There's no branching in Arcade. Every prospect sees the same path, regardless of their role, use case, or company size. Building persona-specific demos means publishing separate Arcade flows for each one.
- **Analytics stop at views.** Step-level drop-off data, CRM integration, and account-level engagement tracking aren't part of what Arcade offers. For teams trying to connect demo engagement to revenue, that's a ceiling.
- **Keeping demos current is manual work.** When your product UI changes, Arcade demos need to be rebuilt step by step. There's no AI-assisted recapture or partial update. For teams shipping product updates regularly, that maintenance overhead compounds fast.
- **Pricing restructured in 2026.** Arcade's pricing changes in 2026 pushed several teams to re-evaluate. Many found they were paying more for a narrower feature set than alternatives offered at a similar or lower price point.


## What happens to your existing Arcade demos?


Your demos carry over. Because Arcade flows are screen-based, the migration is straightforward: share the links, Storylane captures the screens, and a CSM works with you to add the interactive layer on top before anything goes live.


## Step-by-step: switching from Arcade to Storylane


**1. Identify your active Arcade demos**


Start with demos currently embedded on your site, shared in outbound sequences, or used in sales decks. These are your migration priorities. Older or unused demos can wait.


**2. Start a Storylane trial or book a migration call**


Sign up at storylane.io or book a demo directly. For teams with multiple active demos, the migration call gets everything moved over faster with less back-and-forth.


**3. Send your Arcade demo links**


Share the URLs. Storylane's automation captures your screens and rebuilds the guided steps in your workspace.


**4. Review with your CSM**


Your CSM walks through the migrated demos with you. This is where you add branching, configure[lead capture and viewer identification](https://www.storylane.io/blog/guide-to-lead-attribution-for-interactive-demos) , and refine the step-by-step flow. If you've been running the same linear Arcade demo for every buyer, this is the point where you can split it into persona-specific paths.


**5. Replace your embed codes and go live**


Swap the Arcade embed links for Storylane's. Storylane supports[embedding across your full go-to-market stack](https://www.storylane.io/blog/product-demos-on-multiple-platforms) : website, email, outbound sequences, sales decks, and review sites like G2.


## What you gain after switching


- **Demos that feel like the real product.** HTML capture means prospects interact with something that looks and behaves like your actual UI, not a sequence of annotated screenshots. That difference matters when a buyer is trying to understand whether your product fits their workflow.
- **Lead capture and account-level intelligence.** Gate your demo with a form, or identify viewers without gating using Storylane's de-anonymization. Know which companies are watching, how far they got, and where they dropped off. Route those signals directly to your CRM.
- **Branching for different buyer paths.** Build one demo with multiple tracks for different roles, industries, or use cases.[Demo personalization at this level](https://www.storylane.io/blog/demo-personalization-software) means your marketing, sales, and post-sales teams can each have a version built for their audience, managed in one place.
- **Analytics that connect to revenue.** Step-level engagement data, completion rates, and CRM integration give your team the signals to follow up on the right accounts at the right time.
- **Native CRM and marketing integrations.** Storylane connects directly with HubSpot, Salesforce, and your broader GTM stack. Demo engagement data flows into the tools your sales and marketing teams already use, rather than sitting in a separate dashboard no one checks.


If you're still comparing tools before committing, Storylane's[Arcade alternatives guide](https://www.storylane.io/blog/arcade-alternatives) covers the main options by feature, pricing, and use-case fit.


Ready to migrate?[Start a free trial](https://app.storylane.io/signup) or[book a migration call](https://www.storylane.io/request-demo) and your demos can be live in Storylane within days.
